scope: Post-hoc Part 1 GA parameter sensitivity, informed by the completed campaign; one factor at a time, not a full grid. No image work or new MILP solves.
objective: Maximize equal-weight mean full-precision SSIM over all 14 images
baseline_gate: Run baseline 30 first using the same new wrapper and unchanged original solve_ga. Reuse these 30 as the baseline tuning row. Compare all deterministic fields including histories with original trials. Save diagnosis and stop if reproduction differs; never rerun failed seeds.
schedule: Sequential. Baseline gate first; then the four non-baseline settings in cyclic order rotated by seed index, one run per setting per seed. Fresh evaluation alternates baseline/top-non-baseline order by seed index. Baseline timing is earlier than alternative-setting timings, a potential temporal confound.
warmups: One excluded unchanged-GA call per configuration, seed 900000, before baseline gate; retain all outputs. Before fresh evaluation, one excluded call per selected configuration, seed 900001. Warmups are not tuning or final evaluation.
ranking: Highest match count out of 30, then smallest mean absolute SSIM gap, then lowest median runtime_ms; exact residual ties by listed configuration order. Configurations with failed/infeasible runs remain reported but cannot advance to fresh evaluation.
fresh_evaluation: Select highest-ranked non-baseline using only tuning outputs. Save selection before any fresh-seed runs. Run that setting and baseline with the same 30 predefined fresh seeds; retain every result even if improvement disappears.
timing: perf_counter_ns immediately before unchanged solve_ga until it returns; milliseconds. Excludes imports, environment/input loading, shared hash checks, wrapper setup, validation, summaries, plotting and file I/O. Includes algorithm-specific feasibility check, RNG/population initialization, genetic search and result extraction, exactly the original routine timing scope.
invariants: No changes to candidates, floors, budgets, objective, eligibility, initialization rule, tournament selection, uniform crossover, repair, population 100, 200 generations or 20100 evaluations. Only per-gene mutation and elite count vary. More/fewer elites necessarily change offspring and repair-call counts.
limitations: One image batch, one budget, post-hoc tuning. Fresh results are a limited same-problem check, not generalization to other budgets/data, statistical significance, or browser-speed evidence.
